rationale: Clearly above bar. The strongest single signal: in P2 the learner INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED the compounding-error rate as 'sum(n), n=1..T' = O(T^2) for off-policy multi-turn imitation — the classical Ross et al. That is self-arrival at a not-yet-covered result, the reliable above-bar signal for this learner (cf framework-extension evidence). P1 directly recovered the one Read-phase relapse: the Q8 axis-conflation (attributing O(N) density to on-policy) was cleanly corrected — win attributed to Signal density, GRPO (on-policy AND O(1)) offered as the independence counterexample without prompting. P3 applied the map to the learner's own system: chose the data-source flip as the highest-leverage single lever for the 20-50-turn regime (correct — it is the compounding-error axis), named exposure bias / compounding error as the targeted failure mode, and after one push reached the forward-KL trade-off = degrading pre-existing skills (catastrophic forgetting), the §4 headline danger. evidence: P1 attribution recovery (the measured weakness): corrected 'on-policy -> less compute' to 'Signal density = O(N) -> fewer episodes for the same bits -> less compute'; named the axis; produced GRPO (on-policy, O(1)) as the independence counterexample. Directly reverses the Q8 Read-phase conflation.

P2 self-derivation (headline): independently gave the off-policy multi-turn error growth as sum(1..T) = O(T^2) — the DAgger/exposure-bias quadratic, front-running ch-03; contrasted implicitly with the on-policy O(eps*T) linear regime (graded in the states the student actually drifts into).

P2 mechanism assembled: output becomes future input -> an early mistake corrupts the following state -> that state is novel to an off-policy-trained student (teacher never visited it) -> ungraded there, the student errs worse -> recursion.
P2 single-turn contrast (the original framing): correctly isolated why single-turn is harmless — the output never becomes a future input, so the feed-forward loop is absent (T=1, no compounding).

P3(a) prioritization: chose to flip data source (off->on-policy) FIRST as the single highest-leverage lever, because that is the axis that collapses the 20-50-turn compounding error — density is already dense, geometry is secondary to the drift problem.
P3(b) failure mode: named exposure bias / compounding error (the P2 phenomenon) as the specific failure the data-source flip targets.

P3(c) trade-off (reached after one push): leaving geometry at forward-KL keeps mode-covering -> no brake against degrading pre-existing skills (catastrophic forgetting), and forgoes reverse-KL's commit/focus + 'unhackable' property.
Sustained the axis separation under pressure across all three probes — data source vs density vs geometry attributed to the correct axis each time (the central ch-01 objective).
gaps: Axis-attribution was fragile on first pass: the on-policy => O(N) conflation relapsed once in the Read phase (qa Q8) before P1 recovered it under probing. Re-verify at ch-04 (OPD mechanism) and ch-05 (economics), where density-vs-on-policy resurface and the confusion is most tempting.

P2's causal chain needed a hinge scaffold (the 'output becomes the next input' prompt) to assemble; the individual pieces (feed-forward, corrupt state, novel-to-student) and the O(T^2) rate were the learner's, but independent assembly of the full compounding loop was not there on the first attempt. ch-03 (exposure bias / DAgger) is the direct re-probe surface.

P3(c) trade-off required a targeted push to name catastrophic forgetting — the 'commit/focus' half of reverse-KL's value came unprompted, but the §4 headline danger (mode-covering degrades prior capability modes) needed a nudge. Re-probe geometry consequences at ch-04/ch-05.
